name: Walkability Perceptions in Shanghai's New Towns (Pairwise Street Views)
description:
Method replication: same task, scales and design as the paper; the images are not the paper's stimuli (112 Baidu street views re-fetched around the cores of Shanghai's five new towns, Jiading, Qingpu, Songjiang, Fengxian and Nanhui, plus a city-centre and an inner-suburb area; 800×400 px, 120° field of view, level camera, aimed at the side of the street).

Original study: Gong, Huang, White & Langenheim (2023), Land 12(7), 1339. 62 architecture and urban planning students (34 women, 28 men) answered their gender, then chose between two randomly presented Baidu street views from 11 Shanghai communities ("Which place makes you feel the walking environment here is more …?") for five walkability qualities: imageability, enclosure, human scale, complexity and safety. 325 images, 5,474 votes, converted to scores with TrueSkill and compared between women and men.

Differences from the original study: (1) Images are new Baidu views from 7 areas (5 new-town cores and 2 central areas) rather than the paper's 325 images from 11 communities; Baidu's road heading is not always exact, so some views look partly along the street. (2) Each participant answers 12 pairs per quality (60 in total), one quality block after another, instead of an open number of mixed pairs. (3) The short explanation after each quality name is ours. (4) A question on field of study was added so non-student samples can be compared.
author: Gong, Huang, White & Langenheim
